name: IBM Db2
tagline: IBM's enterprise RDBMS for Linux, UNIX, Windows and z/OS, with BLU columnar and pureScale clustering.
description: IBM Db2 is the relational database family behind a large share of mainframe banking and insurance systems, plus a capable Linux/UNIX/Windows edition. Db2 LUW combines BLU Acceleration (in-memory columnar tables) with row-store OLTP, pureScale shared-disk clustering and HADR replication; Db2 for z/OS is a separate code base tuned for Parallel Sysplex. Recent 12.1 mod packs added a vector data type and, in 12.1.5 (June 2026), DiskANN-based vector indexes plus an AI query optimiser. It is technically solid and very stable, but its ecosystem and hiring pool are shrinking outside IBM-centric enterprises.

pricing.notes: Licensed by VPC/core or subscription; free Db2 Community Edition with core and memory limits; Db2 on Cloud and Amazon RDS for Db2 are usage-based.

scale.notes: pureScale (shared-disk) for OLTP scale-out and database partitioning (DPF) for warehouses; HADR for DR.

strengths: BLU Acceleration column-organised tables give fast analytics inside an OLTP database
Adaptive and actual compression routinely cut storage by large factors
pureScale provides active-active clustering on shared storage for continuous availability
Db2 for z/OS is the proven system of record for many of the world's largest banks
SQL compatibility features ease migration from Oracle PL/SQL
weaknesses: Smaller community and tooling ecosystem than PostgreSQL, Oracle or SQL Server
pureScale and z/OS deployments need specialised skills and hardware
Docker Hub images are stale; current containers come from IBM's own registry
useCases: Mainframe core banking and insurance policy systems
SAP and other packaged apps on IBM infrastructure
Operational data warehouses with BLU columnar tables
notIdealFor: Workloads needing a large open-source extension ecosystem
